description: Use this when someone asks whether a company, app or website was hacked or had a data breach, what data leaked, whether a breach notice they received is real, or what to do about a breach they heard of ("Was Canva hacked?", "What leaked in the Ticketmaster breach?"). Searches LeakData's public breach catalog by company, service or domain name and returns each matching breach's date, affected account count, exposed data types, a short summary and the first steps to take. No sign-in is needed. It does not tell whether a particular person's email is in the breach: when emailCheckAvailable is true, offer to check the user's own email with leakdata.search; when it is false, say LeakData cannot check addresses against that breach. When match is "similar", say the name only resembles what the user asked about. No match means the breach is not in LeakData's catalog, not that the company was never breached. If the company is the user's own business or employer, use leakdata.company_monitoring instead. Not for general security news or a person's name.

query.description: Company, app, website or domain name, for example "Canva" or "canva.com". Never an email address, person's name or password.

name: leakdata.breach_lookup

affectedCountIsMinimum.description: affectedAccounts is a reviewed lower bound, not an exact count.

emailCheckAvailable.description: LeakData holds this breach's records, so an email check can find an address in it.

match.description: similar: only the start of the name matched the query, so it may be a different company.

passwordDataTypeCount.description: How many of the first dataTypes are password-type data.

service.description: The site or company to act on; empty for a combined list or malware log.

title: Look up a data breach
